newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Barco 1996 current profit seen up 31 pct.
newsitem.headline: Barco 1996 current profit seen up 31 pct.

text.p: Belgian electronics group Barco NV is expected to post improved 1996 current profit on Wednesday, but analysts were mixed on its share, noting earnings growth would be hit by higher corporate taxes from 1998.
Analysts forecast current net profit for Barco of between 2.7 and 2.9 billion francs ($83.4 million) for 1996/97, up around 31 percent from 2.133 billion in 1995/96.
"Barco will profit from a slowdown in materials costs due to currency translations and improved efficiencies," said analyst Werner Smets at Kredietbank Securities.

Kredietbank pegged 1996 earnings per share (EPS) at 227 francs, up from 201 in 1995. Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL) analyst Erik Theyssens expected EPS for 1996 to reach 242 francs, up from 200 in 1995.
BBL expected Barco's 1996 gross dividend to be around 60 francs, a rise of 20 percent. Kredietbank forecast 65 francs.

Analysts said they expected further strong earnings growth in 1997, but noted that 1998 and 1999 growth in EPS and bottom-line earnings would be slower as Barco's corporate tax rate is due to rise by more than 10 percent over three years.

"There's no easy way out of a higher tax rate of about 30 to 32 percent by 1999 and it will definitely slow down profit growth in 1998/99. But after that there's no reason why Barco should not be able to bring it back into line," said Kredietbank's Smets.
Analysts said Barco was no longer the hot buy it once was, having more than doubled its share price in the past two years, but they remained positive.
Part of Barco's stock rise in the second half of 1996 was linked to speculation on its entry (confirmed in December) into Brussels' Bel-20 leading stock index, they noted.

BBL said at current levels the stock was fairly priced. Compared to the Belgian market it looked expensive but compared with international electronic companies it remained a stock to hold on to, Theyssens said.
More worryingly, analysts said, was Barco's huge cash position. Recent pressure on the stock price had partly been due to market expectations of a large merger not being fulfilled.
"The market is impatient about a Barco acquisition," said analyst Martine Glineur at brokerage Mignon, Hanart, Declerck.
"A significant risk factor at this time is that they have around seven billion Belgian francs cash on the books. This cash is probably only generating 3 to 3.5 percent interest," said Theyssens.
"If they used their cash in a more profitable way by making acquisitions this would immediately have a leverage effect on the bottom-line," Theyssens added.
But KB analyst Smets expected Barco to take its time when considering acquisitions. "They're more interested in quality than speed," he said.

Barco's most recent acquisitions were in January when it bought U.S. privately-held projector maker Electronic Image System Inc (EIS) and set up units in India for research and development and for sales and marketing of projectors.
